// max_grid_size: 361, ruled by the coordinator on 2026-08-27 (resolution 2) and MEASURED rather than defaulted. At z11 a GLO-30 tile edge carries ~316 one-arcsecond posts (the run reports it per level as sourcePostsPerTileEdge), so a 361-post lattice resolves the source there and 217 under-resolved it by 1.46x; at z10 the source carries 633 and neither lattice resolves it. That ratio no longer decides what the ACCURACY figure means — the encoder measures every record against the source posts themselves (resolution 1) whatever the lattice does — but it decides what the density ladder can BUY: the divisors of 360 give the ladder 5, 6, 7, 9, 10, 11, 13, 16, 19, 21, 25, 31, 37, 41, 46, 61, 73, 91, 121, 181, 361, so a tile that needs a little more than 73 posts can buy 91 instead of jumping to 109 and past the byte bound. The A/B half is kept at regions/liguria-z11-lattice217.json: build it into its own --out and compare the two verify reports.
